title: 7.1 Simplifying and Verifying Trigonometric Identities
objectives: Simplify trigonometric expressions using algebra and the identities.
headings: Using Algebra to Simplify Trigonometric Expressions

items.title: Example 1
items.prompt_text: Graphing the Expressions of an Identity Graph both sides of the identity $cot \theta = \frac{1}{tan \theta} .$ In other words, on the graphing calculator, graph $y = cot \theta$ and $y = \frac{1}{tan \theta} .$

items.title: Example 2
items.prompt_text: Verifying a Trigonometric Identity Verify $tan \theta cos \theta = sin \theta .$

items.title: Try It #1
items.prompt_text: Verify the identity $csc \theta cos \theta tan \theta = 1.$

items.title: Example 3
items.prompt_text: Verifying the Equivalency Using the Even-Odd Identities Verify the following equivalency using the even-odd identities: $(1 + sin x) \left[\right. 1 + sin (- x) \left]\right. = cos^{2} x$
prompt_latex_bits: (1 + sin x) \left[\right. 1 + sin (- x) \left]\right. = cos^{2} x

items.title: Example 4
items.nearest_heading: Verifying the Equivalency Using the Even-Odd Identities
items.prompt_text: Verifying a Trigonometric Identity Involving sec 2 θ Verify the identity $\frac{sec^{2} \theta - 1}{sec^{2} \theta} = sin^{2} \theta$

items.title: Try It #2
items.prompt_text: Show that $\frac{cot \theta}{csc \theta} = cos \theta .$

items.title: Example 5
items.prompt_text: Creating and Verifying an Identity Create an identity for the expression $2 tan \theta sec \theta$ by rewriting strictly in terms of sine.

items.title: Example 6
items.prompt_text: Verifying an Identity Using Algebra and Even/Odd Identities Verify the identity: $\frac{sin^{2} \left(\right. - \theta \left.\right) - cos^{2} \left(\right. - \theta \left.\right)}{sin \left(\right. - \theta \left.\right) - cos \left(\right. - \theta \left.\right)} = cos \theta - sin \theta$

items.title: Try It #3
items.prompt_text: Verify the identity $\frac{sin^{2} \theta - 1}{tan \theta sin \theta - tan \theta} = \frac{sin \theta + 1}{tan \theta} .$

items.title: Example 7
items.prompt_text: Verifying an Identity Involving Cosines and Cotangents Verify the identity: $\left(\right. 1 - cos^{2} x \left.\right) \left(\right. 1 + cot^{2} x \left.\right) = 1.$

items.title: Example 8
items.nearest_heading: Using Algebra to Simplify Trigonometric Expressions
items.prompt_text: Writing the Trigonometric Expression as an Algebraic Expression Write the following trigonometric expression as an algebraic expression: $2 cos^{2} \theta + cos \theta - 1.$

items.title: Example 9
items.nearest_heading: Writing the Trigonometric Expression as an Algebraic Expression
items.prompt_text: Rewriting a Trigonometric Expression Using the Difference of Squares Rewrite the trigonometric expression: $4 cos^{2} \theta - 1.$

items.title: Try It #4
items.prompt_text: Rewrite the trigonometric expression: $25 - 9 sin^{2} \theta .$

items.title: Example 10
items.prompt_text: Simplify by Rewriting and Using Substitution Simplify the expression by rewriting and using identities: $csc^{2} \theta - cot^{2} \theta$

items.title: Try It #5
items.prompt_text: Use algebraic techniques to verify the identity: $\frac{cos \theta}{1 + sin \theta} = \frac{1 - sin \theta}{cos \theta} .$ (Hint: Multiply the numerator and denominator on the left side by $1 - sin \theta . \left.\right)$

1 . We know $g (x) = cos x$ is an even function, and $f (x) = sin x$ and $h (x) = tan x$ are odd functions. What about $G (x) = cos^{2} x , F (x) = sin^{2} x ,$ and $H (x) = tan^{2} x ?$ Are they even, odd, or neither? Why?
prompt_latex_bits: G (x) = cos^{2} x , F (x) = sin^{2} x ,

items.prompt_text: 2 . Examine the graph of $f (x) = sec x$ on the interval $\left[\right. - \pi , \pi \left]\right. .$ How can we tell whether the function is even or odd by only observing the graph of $f (x) = sec x ?$
3 . After examining the reciprocal identity for $sec t ,$ explain why the function is undefined at certain points.
4 . All of the Pythagorean Identities are related. Describe how to manipulate the equations to get from $sin^{2} t + cos^{2} t = 1$ to the other forms.
